transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (joined late), Meera (Hightower Head of Platform), Daniel (SRE), Alicia (Security)

Summary (auto): Discussed reliability requirements, fallback policies, multi-region routing, and next steps for benchmark and security review.

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro - im Sofia, i'm the AE on this account, with me is Ethan our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Meera: good thanks, we've had a few meetings internally and excited to understand how Redwood would handle incidents at scale, esp around multi-region failover.
[00:16] Ethan: great, yeah i'll try to cover runtime behaviour and routing. quick ask first - can you share top of mind constraints? latency targets, regions, and whether you're leaning hosted/dedicated/private?
[00:28] Daniel: sure, our primary region is us-east-1, secondary eu-west-1. target p99 latency for inference is sub 250ms for our m2 flow, we do bursts up to 1200 rps during peak campaigns.
[00:40] Meera: also important - we need predictable failover: if a region degrades we want automatic routing to secondary without large error rates. and clear SLA terms.
[00:50] Alicia: security side: SOC2 type II must be presented, we need customer-managed KMS keys for private deployments ideally, and audit logs shipped for 1 year. also SSO (SAML) for console.
[01:05] Ethan: makes sense. quick overview - Redwood supports Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). each has different tradeoffs. Hosted is fastest to try, but dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and more control, private gives full network isolation and can use your KMS.
[01:20] Meera: if we start hosted, can we guarantee region affinity and failover policies? we cant afford cold fallback that triples latency.
[01:28] Sofia: breakdown - Redwood's routing policy can pin by region, and we have multi-region routing rules. typical setup: primary route to us-east, health checks + circuit breaker, then automatic fallback to eu-west if latency/availability thresholds are hit. the fallback path depends on whether models are pinned - if eu-west runs a smaller model variant you'll see different latencies.
[01:45] Daniel: what about model compatibility? if primary uses fp16 quantized variant and fallback is a more quantized run, does output quality change? we care about correctness for fraud scoring.
[01:55] Ethan: yes there can be quality delta. our suggestions: configure model variant chains - prefer same model version across regions where possible; if not, set automatic rerank or post-processing to normalize outputs. we also support structured failure responses so your app can degrade gracefully.
[02:12] Meera: and about traffic bursts - do you do queuing or shedding? we cant have long queues at p99.
[02:19] Ethan: we do workload-aware batching but with latency SLOs enforced; plus a circuit breaker that will route to lower-latency capacity or to a lower-cost variant rather than queuing indefinitely. for Dedicated customers you can reserve burst capacity to avoid shedding.
[02:34] Alicia: on encryption - you mentioned customer-managed KMS only in private? what about dedicated?
[02:39] Sofia: dedicated supports customer-managed keys for data at rest in many cases; for Hosted we have encryption at rest but CMK support is available with enterprise contracts. private gives the most control (bring-your-own KMS/HSM).
[02:53] Meera: can you explain SLO vs SLA mapping - we have internal SLOs (p99 < 250ms, availability 99.9%). we need to know what Redwood can commit to and what happens on violation.
[03:04] Ethan: SLAs are explicit on Dedicated and Private - typically 99.95% for Dedicated with credits on breach; Hosted has best-effort SLAs for self-serve tiers and clearer SLAs for enterprise tenants. for incident tolerance we provide automated fallback + multi-region routing, but the SLA also depends on the configuration - e.g., if you pin to a single-region model, that impacts failover.
[03:25] Daniel: in a full region outage, what's the expected RTO for failover? like seconds, minutes?
[03:30] Ethan: typical failover we see is sub 60 seconds for routing if health checks are configured aggressively; full warmup if model weights need to be loaded in the fallback region can be a few minutes unless you pre-warm or maintain a standing replica. Dedicated can keep standby replicas to reduce RTO to under 30s.
[03:47] Meera: pre-warming reps is doable but expensive. how does Redwood recommend balancing cost vs RTO?
[03:54] Sofia: options: 1) cross-region warm replicas (higher cost, lowest RTO), 2) keep smaller quantized models warmed as fallbacks (cheaper, slightly different quality), 3) use lightweight routing to direct small % of traffic to secondary to keep it warm. Redwood Optimize can recommend cost-effective configs.
[04:12] Alicia: audit logs - do you provide token-level request logs and can they be exported to our SIEM?
[04:17] Ethan: yes audit & detailed request logs are available; we can stream to your S3/CloudWatch or push to Splunk/Datadog. retention configurable; enterprise customers often choose 12 months.
[04:26] Tom: curious about reroutes during partial degradation - do you do gradual traffic shifting or abrupt cutover? we want canary-style failover to avoid spike overload.
[04:34] Ethan: we support progressive traffic shifting - canary + percent-based rollouts, and automatic circuit-breaker thresholds that will shift traffic proportionally. + health-based throttling so the secondary isn't overwhelmed.
[04:46] Meera: do you have observability hooks we can integrate into our SRE dashboards?
[04:50] Ethan: yes per-route/model dashboards, token-level latency breakdown, traces. we also emit events when fallback triggers and can add tracing headers to requests to correlate.
[05:00] Meera: any real-world examples of region failover?
[05:03] Sofia: one of our retail customers had a provider-level fault in us-east, they had a dedicated setup with warm replicas in eu-west; failover occurred within 45s and error rate was <0.5% because they had progressive shifting and pre-warmed smaller fallback models.
[05:16] Daniel: about testing - we'd like Redwood to run a POC simulating region outage and show metrics.
[05:21] Sofia: yes we can run a benchmark / POC. typically we ask for: sample payloads, target qps, SLOs, and locations. we can demonstrate routing, fallback, and show latencies, error rates, and recovery time.
[05:33] Alicia: compliance - does Redwood provide SOC2 report and ISO27001? also penetration testing attestations?
[05:39] Sofia: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts; penetration testing results summary available under NDA. i'll include the pack in the follow-up.
[05:47] Meera: what about data residency - we need to ensure EU customer data stays in region for some flows. can routing be tag-based?
[05:55] Ethan: yes we support routing polices based on metadata - region tags, tenant tags - you can route EU traffic to eu-west and block fallback to outside EU for those workloads. that's a config option in Private/Dedicated and available in Hosted with enterprise settings.
[06:10] Daniel: failure modes - if the control plane loses visibility of a region, do clients receive 5xx errors or a structured fallback response?
[06:16] Ethan: we return structured fallback responses when possible; for request-level errors we use retry + fallback chains. we also provide SDK client libraries that implement recommended retry/backoff to avoid cascading failures.
[06:28] Meera: how are KV caches handled in cross-region failover? last thing we want is cache-on-Miss spikes.
[06:33] Ethan: KV cache is local to region; we support prefix caching and can replicate hot keys across regions for critical state. for stateless models we mitigate by warming. if you need strong cache consistency, we'd recommend Private with a cross-region replicated cache you control.
[06:49] Sofia: one nuance - some transcriptions or logs we saw mention K-V cash - sorry autocorrect, but yes it's KV cache.
[06:55] (brief laugh)
[07:00] Meera: ok on costs - if we keep warm replicas in secondary region what's the expected uplift? ballpark.
[07:05] Sofia: depends on model size. warm replica for a 13B model could be ~30-40% uplift relative to primary compute cost; smaller quantized fallbacks much lower. Redwood Optimize can run a model-sizing report for your workload to give exact numbers.
[07:20] Tom: are there throttles per tenant - we have multiple internal teams, can we set per-route quotas?
[07:25] Ethan: yes multi-tenant routing, per-API-key quotas and per-route rate limits are supported; plus you can set guaranteed throughput on Dedicated capacity.
[07:34] Daniel: about error budgets - if there's an SLA credit, how is that calculated?
[07:38] Sofia: typical credit calculation is tied to monthly uptime percentage. we'll share the detailed SLA doc - but credits are pro-rata and applied as account credits; specifics differ by contract.
[07:49] Meera: one more question - in the event of a cascading cloud provider issue that affects multiple regions, do you have cross-provider failover or is it within the same cloud?
[07:58] Ethan: we support multi-cloud routing; many customers run backups in another cloud region as an extreme case. Redwood's control plane can route across providers; for private setups you can orchestrate across your own infra. multi-cloud adds complexity for network egress and data residency but it's supported.
[08:14] Priya (joined late): hey everyone, sorry running a bit behind - quick note on warmup strategies: we also do lightweight warmers that only load tokenizer and partial weights to reduce memory/warmup time.
[08:24] Alicia: good to know.
[08:28] Meera: ok to recap, we need: security pack (SOC2/ISO), a POC simulating us-east outage, and cost estimates for warm replicas. we'll also share traffic profile and SLOs.
[08:40] Sofia: perfect. we'll send over the docs and propose dates for a POC. Ethan will own the benchmark run.
[08:47] Daniel: fine by us. any pitfalls to highlight?
[08:50] Ethan: watch out for model variant drift - ensure deterministic evaluation sets are used across regions. Redwood can help with eval harnesses so your fraud rules behave consistently.
[09:01] Meera: thanks, that addresses most concerns. let's plan to reconvene after you share the pack.
[09:07] Sofia: great thanks everyone. end.
